  \begin{block}{Data}
    {\small
    \begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.38\linewidth}p{0.57\linewidth}@{}}
      \toprule
      \textbf{Source} & \textbf{Content} \\
      \midrule
      WRI ESB Dataset v9  & All-source ESB adoption; delivery dates \\
      EPA CSB Rebates     & R1 (2022) \& R3 (2023) lottery winners \\
      CSBP Applicants     & Waitlisted/rejected by round \\
      NCES EDGE           & District shapefiles + centroids \\
      NCES CCD / ACS      & Enrollment, income, poverty, race \\
      NASA SEDAC          & PM\textsubscript{2.5} \\
      MIT Election Lab    & 2020 county presidential vote \\
      \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    }
    \vskip0.5ex
    {\small\textbf{Sample:} 12,388 non-R1-winner districts.
    \textbf{Geography:} K\,=\,6 nearest neighbors (EPSG:5070).}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1.5ex

  %-- Identification ----------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Identification Challenge}
    \textbf{The reflection problem} (Manski, 1993): contemporaneous peer
    adoption is simultaneously determined — OLS is biased and inconsistent.

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{This paper's fix — temporal design:}
    Use \textbf{Round 1 (2022)} lottery randomness to predict neighbor bus
    deployment \emph{visible} before \textbf{Round 3 (2023)} application
    decisions.

    \vskip1ex
    \begin{center}
    \begin{tikzpicture}[
        node distance = 2.0cm,
        box/.style   = {rectangle, rounded corners=4pt,
                        draw=SlateBlue, fill=LightGrey,
                        text width=3.0cm, align=center,
                        minimum height=1.0cm, font=\small},
        arr/.style   = {-Stealth, thick, color=BCMaroon},
        lbl/.style   = {font=\footnotesize\itshape, color=SlateBlue}
      ]
      \node[box] (r1)  {R1 Lottery\\Oct 2022};
      \node[box, right=of r1]  (del) {R1 Bus\\Deliveries\\2022--2023};
      \node[box, right=of del] (r3)  {R3 Application\\Oct 2023};

      \draw[arr] (r1)  -- node[above,lbl]{$Z$: lottery} (del);
      \draw[arr] (del) -- node[above,lbl]{visibility} (r3);

      \draw[->, dashed, thick, color=ESBGreen,
            bend right=40, looseness=0.8]
        (del.south) to
        node[below, lbl, text width=2.8cm, align=center]
        {peer observes\\operating ESB}
        (r3.south);
    \end{tikzpicture}
    \end{center}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Key validity conditions:}
    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.1ex}
      \item Lottery is random within \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} strata
            (confirmed from program guide).
      \item Neighbor loser-density control ($w_6$\,\textit{IS\_R1\_LOSER})
            absorbs geographic application-clustering.
      \item $Z$ affects $Y$ only through neighbor deployment (exclusion
            restriction).
    \end{itemize}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1.5ex

  %-- Lottery structure -------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Lottery Structure: 6-Tier Stratified Draw}
    {\small Random \emph{within} \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} cells;
    win rates differ \emph{between} cells by design.}

    \vskip0.4ex
    {\small
    \begin{tabular}{@{}cl@{}}
      \toprule Tier & Pool \\ \midrule
      1 & ZE priority districts — per state \\
      2 & Clean priority districts — per state \\
      3 & All remaining priority districts \\
      4 & Non-priority clean districts \\
      5 & Remaining priority ZE \\
      6 & Remaining non-priority ZE \\
      \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    }

    \vskip0.5ex
    {\small$\Rightarrow$ FE: \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} interactions
    ($\approx$100 dummies) for within-strata comparisons.}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1.5ex

  %-- Estimating equations ----------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Estimating Equations}

    \textbf{Reduced form (ITT):}
    \vskip0.2ex
    $Y_i^{R3} = \alpha + \delta\,\bar{Z}_i^{K=6} + \rho\,\bar{L}_i^{K=6}
               + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s} + \varepsilon_i$

    \vskip0.3ex
    {\small $Y_i^{R3}=\mathbf{1}[\text{applied to R3}]$;\;
    $\bar{Z}_i$ = neighbor R1 winner share;\;
    $\bar{L}_i$ = neighbor R1 loser share.}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Structural 2SLS:}
    \vskip0.2ex
    {\small FS:\;$\hat{D}_i = \pi\,\bar{Z}_i + \phi\,\bar{L}_i + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s}$}\\[0.3ex]
    {\small SS:\;$Y_i^{R3} = \alpha + \beta^{\scriptscriptstyle IV}\hat{D}_i
                 + \rho\,\bar{L}_i + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s} + u_i$}\\[0.2ex]
    {\small $D_i$ = neighbor share with WRI-tracked ESB by end of 2023.}
  \end{block}

\end{column}

%====================================================================
%  COLUMN 3 — Results
%====================================================================
\begin{column}{\sepwid}\end{column}
\begin{column}{\onecolwid}

  %-- Main result -------------------------------------------------
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted title}{fg=white, bg=ESBGreen}
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted body} {fg=black, bg=LightGrey}
  \begin{alertblock}{Main Result: Application Margin (Estimand 2)}

    \textbf{Outcome:} $Y_i^{R3} = \mathbf{1}[\text{applied to R3 lottery}]$

    \vskip0.8ex
    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}
    \begin{tabular}{lrrrrr}
      \toprule
      Specification & $N$ & $\hat\delta$ & SE & $t$ & $p$ \\
      \midrule
      K\,=\,6, with loser ctrl  & 12,388 & $+0.051$ & 0.029 & 1.75 & 0.081 \\
      K\,=\,10, with loser ctrl & 12,388 & $+0.081$ & 0.043 & 1.90 & 0.058 \\
      \midrule
      \textbf{Priority subsample, K\,=\,6}
        & \textbf{6,402} & $\mathbf{+0.119}$ & \textbf{0.051}
        & \textbf{2.36} & \textbf{0.019} \\
      \bottomrule
      \multicolumn{6}{l}{\footnotesize State-clustered SE.\;
        Controls: log enroll., log income, poverty,}\\
      \multicolumn{6}{l}{\footnotesize \%\,white, PM$_{2.5}$, \%\,Dem\,2020,
        priority\,$\times$\,state FE.}\\
    \end{tabular}
    \end{adjustbox}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Interpretation:} An additional R1-winning neighbor raises own R3
    application probability by $\approx\!3$\,pp (full) to $\approx\!7$\,pp
    (priority districts).
  \end{alertblock}

  \vskip2ex

  %-- OLS vs 2SLS -------------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{OLS Naive vs.\ Structural 2SLS}

    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}
    \begin{tabular}{lrrrrr}
      \toprule
      Estimator & $\hat\beta$ & SE & $p$ & AR $p(\beta\!=\!0)$ & AR 95\% CI \\
      \midrule
      OLS (naive)          & $-0.040$ & 0.011 & $<$0.001 & — & — \\
      2SLS, full, K\,=\,6  & $+1.281$ & 0.928 & 0.167 & 0.087 & $[-0.18,\;7.03]$ \\
      2SLS, priority, K\,=\,6 & $+3.057$ & 2.093 & 0.144
        & \textbf{0.023} & $\mathbf{[+0.43,\;\infty)}$ \\
      \bottomrule
      \multicolumn{6}{l}{\footnotesize FS\,$F=7.06$ (K\,=\,6).\;
        AR\,=\,Anderson-Rubin weak-IV-robust CI.}\\
    \end{tabular}
    \end{adjustbox}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.2ex}
      \item \textbf{OLS sign flip} reveals selection bias: more-saturated
            local markets have lower marginal motivation to apply.
      \item \textbf{2SLS corrects} this; weak FS ($F\!=\!7.06$) makes AR
            CI the credible reference for inference.
      \item \textbf{Priority AR CI excludes zero}: structural effect is
            robustly positive even under weak-IV inference.
    \end{itemize}
  \end{block}

  \vskip2ex

  %-- Null benchmarks ---------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Null Benchmarks — Adoption Outcomes}
    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}
    \begin{tabular}{lrr}
      \toprule
      Outcome (K\,=\,6, loser ctrl) & $\hat\delta$ & $p$ \\
      \midrule
      CSBP adoption ITT          & $+0.007$ & 0.780 \\
      All-source WRI 2023--24    & $+0.018$ & 0.567 \\
      All-source WRI 2024 only   & $+0.004$ & 0.872 \\
      \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    \end{adjustbox}
    \vskip0.6ex
    {\small The peer effect is \textbf{specific to programme entry} —
    consistent with a window too short for deployment to drive observable
    adoption changes. Fiscal constraints may prevent interest from completing
    into ownership.}
  \end{block}

  \vskip2ex

  %-- Mechanism ---------------------------------------------------
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted title}{fg=white, bg=AmberGold}
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted body} {fg=black, bg=LightGrey}
  \begin{alertblock}{Mechanism: Timing-Sensitive Information Channel}

    \textbf{Sharp cutoff:} R3 deadline = October 2023.\\
    Split R1 deliveries: \textit{pre\_r3} ($\leq$2023\,Q3, \emph{visible})
    vs.\ \textit{post\_r3} ($\geq$2023\,Q4, \emph{invisible}).

    \vskip0.5ex
    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}
    \begin{tabular}{lrrrr}
      \toprule
      Timing & $\hat\eta$ & SE & $p$ & Direction \\
      \midrule
      \textit{pre\_r3} (visible)   & $+0.092$ & 0.054 & 0.091* & $\uparrow$ \\
      \textit{post\_r3} (invisible) & $-0.012$ & 0.072 & 0.865  & $\downarrow$ \\
      \midrule
      \multicolumn{5}{l}{\footnotesize Priority subsample.\;
        Wald (pre\,=\,post): $p = 0.239$.}\\
      \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    \end{adjustbox}

    \vskip0.5ex
    {\small Pre-deadline neighbors (buses \emph{visible} at time of decision)
    raise application rates; post-deadline neighbors do not.
    Post\_r3 is positive for \emph{adoption} outcomes — no generalised
    deterrence, only a deadline-sensitive information channel.}
  \end{alertblock}

\end{column}

%====================================================================
%  COLUMN 4 — Maps + Conclusions
%====================================================================
\begin{column}{\sepwid}\end{column}
\begin{column}{\onecolwid}

  %-- Program map -------------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Figure 2: R1 Winners and R3 Applicants}
    \begin{figure}
      \includegraphics[width=\linewidth,keepaspectratio]
        {map_01_national_overview.png}
      \caption{Panel A: R1 lottery winners (green). Panel B: R3 applicants
               who did not win R1 (orange). Application is concentrated in
               the South and Mid-Atlantic — identification relies on
               \emph{within-state, within-strata} variation.}
    \end{figure}
  \end{block}

  \vskip2ex

  %-- California zoom ---------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Figure 3: California — Delivery Timing and R3 Activity}
    \begin{figure}
      \includegraphics[width=\linewidth,keepaspectratio]
        {map_03_california_zoom.png}
      \caption{Left: R1 winner districts by delivery timing (green =
               pre-deadline; red = post-deadline). Right: R3 applicants.
               Pre-deadline deliveries are sparse; R3 application nonetheless
               occurs nearby, consistent with the information channel.}
    \end{figure}
  \end{block}

  \vskip2ex

  %-- Conclusions -------------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Conclusions \& Policy Implications}
    \begin{enumerate}\setlength\itemsep{0.5ex}
      \item \textbf{Peer effects at the application margin:} A lottery-winning
            neighbor raises R3 application propensity by $\sim$3--7\,pp
            (5--12\,pp for priority-eligible districts, $p<0.02$).
      \item \textbf{Structural effect positive for priority districts:}
            2SLS Anderson-Rubin CI excludes zero ($p=0.023$); OLS
            sign-flip confirms downward selection bias.
      \item \textbf{Timing-sensitive information channel:} Only
            \emph{pre-deadline} neighbor deployments generate spillovers;
            post-deadline buses have no detectable effect on application
            behavior.
      \item \textbf{No adoption spillovers (yet):} Null results for
            all-source WRI adoption suggest the 15-month window is too
            short for ownership-level peer effects to materialize.
    \end{enumerate}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Policy implication:} Expediting delivery and creating visible
    demonstration fleets could amplify federal ESB investment by triggering
    peer-induced demand in subsequent lottery rounds.

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textit{Next steps:} longer diffusion windows (2025--26 data);
    mechanism decomposition (vendor networks vs.\ direct information);
    heterogeneity by urbanicity.
  \end{block}

\end{column}
\begin{column}{\sepwid}\end{column}

\end{columns}

  \begin{block}{Identification Challenge}
    \textbf{The reflection problem} (Manski, 1993): contemporaneous peer
    adoption is simultaneously determined — OLS is biased and inconsistent.

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{This paper's fix — temporal design:}
    Use \textbf{Round 1 (2022)} lottery randomness to predict neighbor bus
    deployment \emph{visible} before \textbf{Round 3 (2023)} application
    decisions.

    \begin{center}

    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.1ex}
      \item Lottery is random within \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} strata
            (confirmed from program guide).
      \item Neighbor loser-density control ($w_6$\,\textit{IS\_R1\_LOSER})
            absorbs geographic application-clustering.
      \item $Z$ affects $Y$ only through neighbor deployment (exclusion
            restriction).
    \end{itemize}
  \end{block}

  \begin{block}{Lottery Structure: 6-Tier Stratified Draw}
    {\small Random \emph{within} \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} cells;

    \vskip0.4ex
    {\small
    \begin{tabular}{@{}cl@{}}

  %-- Estimating equations ----------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Estimating Equations}

    \textbf{Reduced form (ITT):}
    \vskip0.2ex
    $Y_i^{R3} = \alpha + \delta\,\bar{Z}_i^{K=6} + \rho\,\bar{L}_i^{K=6}
               + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s} + \varepsilon_i$

    \vskip0.3ex
    {\small $Y_i^{R3}=\mathbf{1}[\text{applied to R3}]$;\;
    $\bar{Z}_i$ = neighbor R1 winner share;\;
    $\bar{L}_i$ = neighbor R1 loser share.}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Structural 2SLS:}
    \vskip0.2ex
    {\small FS:\;$\hat{D}_i = \pi\,\bar{Z}_i + \phi\,\bar{L}_i + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s}$}\\[0.3ex]
    {\small SS:\;$Y_i^{R3} = \alpha + \beta^{\scriptscriptstyle IV}\hat{D}_i
                 + \rho\,\bar{L}_i + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s} + u_i$}\\[0.2ex]
    {\small $D_i$ = neighbor share with WRI-tracked ESB by end of 2023.}
  \end{block}

    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}

      \toprule

      \midrule

      2SLS, full, K\,=\,6  & $+1.281$ & 0.928 & 0.167 & 0.087 & $[-0.18,\;7.03]$ \\
      2SLS, priority, K\,=\,6 & $+3.057$ & 2.093 & 0.144
        & \textbf{0.023} & $\mathbf{[+0.43,\;\infty)}$ \\
      \bottomrule

    \end{tabular}
    \end{adjustbox}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.2ex}
      \item \textbf{OLS sign flip} reveals selection bias: more-saturated

  \vskip2ex

  %-- Conclusions -------------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Conclusions \& Policy Implications}
    \begin{enumerate}\setlength\itemsep{0.5ex}
      \item \textbf{Peer effects at the application margin:} A lottery-winning
            neighbor raises R3 application propensity by $\sim$3--7\,pp
            (5--12\,pp for priority-eligible districts, $p<0.02$).
      \item \textbf{Structural effect positive for priority districts:}
            2SLS Anderson-Rubin CI excludes zero ($p=0.023$); OLS
            sign-flip confirms downward selection bias.
      \item \textbf{Timing-sensitive information channel:} Only
            \emph{pre-deadline} neighbor deployments generate spillovers;
            post-deadline buses have no detectable effect on application
            behavior.
      \item \textbf{No adoption spillovers (yet):} Null results for
            all-source WRI adoption suggest the 15-month window is too
            short for ownership-level peer effects to materialize.
    \end{enumerate}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Policy implication:} Expediting delivery and creating visible
    demonstration fleets could amplify federal ESB investment by triggering
    peer-induced demand in subsequent lottery rounds.

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textit{Next steps:} longer diffusion windows (2025--26 data);
    mechanism decomposition (vendor networks vs.\ direct information);
    heterogeneity by urbanicity.
  \end{block}

  \setbeamercolor{block alerted title}{fg=white, bg=BCMaroon}
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted body} {fg=black, bg=LightGrey}
  \begin{alertblock}{Why Electric School Buses?}
    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.2ex}
      \item $\approx\!500{,}000$ diesel school buses in the U.S.\ — the largest
            source of diesel pollution exposure for children.
      \item Federal \textbf{Clean School Bus Program} (CSBP, EPA, 2022):
            lottery-based rebates for electric/clean bus replacement.
      \item Adoption is geographically clustered (Figure~1) — some districts
            act early; most never apply. Why?
    \end{itemize}
    \vskip0.4em
    \textbf{Central question:} Does observing a \emph{neighbor district's}
    electric bus deployment increase your own probability of seeking adoption?
  \end{alertblock}

  \vskip1.5ex

    \end{figure}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1.5ex

  %-- Literature --------------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Related Literature}
    {\small
    \textbf{Peer effects / social learning in adoption:}
    Conley \& Udry (2010); Bollinger \& Gillingham (2012);
    Noll et al.\ (2014); Bos et al.\ (2021)\\[0.3ex]
    \textbf{Reflection problem \& IV:}
    Manski (1993); Bram\-oulle et al.\ (2009)\\[0.3ex]
    \textbf{Environmental \& energy adoption:}
    Kahn \& Ketcham (2021); Ryan \& Tucker (2012)
    }
  \end{block}

\end{column}

%====================================================================
%  COLUMN 2 — Data + Identification
%====================================================================
\begin{column}{\sepwid}\end{column}
\begin{column}{\onecolwid}

  %-- Data (compact) ----------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Data}
    {\small
    \begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.38\linewidth}p{0.57\linewidth}@{}}
      \toprule
      \textbf{Source} & \textbf{Content} \\
      \midrule
      WRI ESB Dataset v9  & All-source ESB adoption; delivery dates \\
      EPA CSB Rebates     & R1 (2022) \& R3 (2023) lottery winners \\
      CSBP Applicants     & Waitlisted/rejected by round \\
      NCES EDGE           & District shapefiles + centroids \\
      NCES CCD / ACS      & Enrollment, income, poverty, race \\
      NASA SEDAC          & PM\textsubscript{2.5} \\
      MIT Election Lab    & 2020 county presidential vote \\
      \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    }
    \vskip0.5ex
    {\small\textbf{Sample:} 12,388 non-R1-winner districts.
    \textbf{Geography:} K\,=\,6 nearest neighbors (EPSG:5070).}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1.5ex

  %-- Identification ----------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Identification Challenge}
    \textbf{The reflection problem} (Manski, 1993): contemporaneous peer
    adoption is simultaneously determined — OLS is biased and inconsistent.

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{This paper's fix — temporal design:}
    Use \textbf{Round 1 (2022)} lottery randomness to predict neighbor bus
    deployment \emph{visible} before \textbf{Round 3 (2023)} application
    decisions.

    \vskip1ex
    \begin{center}
    \begin{tikzpicture}[
        node distance = 2.0cm,
        box/.style   = {rectangle, rounded corners=4pt,
                        draw=SlateBlue, fill=LightGrey,
                        text width=3.0cm, align=center,
                        minimum height=1.0cm, font=\small},
        arr/.style   = {-Stealth, thick, color=BCMaroon},
        lbl/.style   = {font=\footnotesize\itshape, color=SlateBlue}
      ]
      \node[box] (r1)  {R1 Lottery\\Oct 2022};
      \node[box, right=of r1]  (del) {R1 Bus\\Deliveries\\2022--2023};
      \node[box, right=of del] (r3)  {R3 Application\\Oct 2023};

      \draw[arr] (r1)  -- node[above,lbl]{$Z$: lottery} (del);
      \draw[arr] (del) -- node[above,lbl]{visibility} (r3);

      \draw[->, dashed, thick, color=ESBGreen,
            bend right=40, looseness=0.8]
        (del.south) to
        node[below, lbl, text width=2.8cm, align=center]
        {peer observes\\operating ESB}
        (r3.south);
    \end{tikzpicture}
    \end{center}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Key validity conditions:}
    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.1ex}
      \item Lottery is random within \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} strata
            (confirmed from program guide).
      \item Neighbor loser-density control ($w_6$\,\textit{IS\_R1\_LOSER})
            absorbs geographic application-clustering.
      \item $Z$ affects $Y$ only through neighbor deployment (exclusion
            restriction).
    \end{itemize}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1.5ex

  %-- Lottery structure -------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Lottery Structure: 6-Tier Stratified Draw}
    {\small Random \emph{within} \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} cells;
    win rates differ \emph{between} cells by design.}

    \vskip0.4ex
    {\small
    \begin{tabular}{@{}cl@{}}
      \toprule Tier & Pool \\ \midrule
      1 & ZE priority districts — per state \\
      2 & Clean priority districts — per state \\
      3 & All remaining priority districts \\
      4 & Non-priority clean districts \\
      5 & Remaining priority ZE \\
      6 & Remaining non-priority ZE \\
      \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    }

    \vskip0.5ex
    {\small$\Rightarrow$ FE: \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} interactions
    ($\approx$100 dummies) for within-strata comparisons.}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1.5ex

  %-- Estimating equations ----------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Estimating Equations}

    \textbf{Reduced form (ITT):}
    \vskip0.2ex
    $Y_i^{R3} = \alpha + \delta\,\bar{Z}_i^{K=6} + \rho\,\bar{L}_i^{K=6}
               + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s} + \varepsilon_i$

    \vskip0.3ex
    {\small $Y_i^{R3}=\mathbf{1}[\text{applied to R3}]$;\;
    $\bar{Z}_i$ = neighbor R1 winner share;\;
    $\bar{L}_i$ = neighbor R1 loser share.}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Structural 2SLS:}
    \vskip0.2ex
    {\small FS:\;$\hat{D}_i = \pi\,\bar{Z}_i + \phi\,\bar{L}_i + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s}$}\\[0.3ex]
    {\small SS:\;$Y_i^{R3} = \alpha + \beta^{\scriptscriptstyle IV}\hat{D}_i
                 + \rho\,\bar{L}_i + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s} + u_i$}\\[0.2ex]
    {\small $D_i$ = neighbor share with WRI-tracked ESB by end of 2023.}
  \end{block}

\end{column}

%====================================================================
%  COLUMN 3 — Results
%====================================================================
\begin{column}{\sepwid}\end{column}
\begin{column}{\onecolwid}

  %-- Main result -------------------------------------------------
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted title}{fg=white, bg=ESBGreen}
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted body} {fg=black, bg=LightGrey}
  \begin{alertblock}{Main Result: Application Margin (Estimand 2)}

    \textbf{Outcome:} $Y_i^{R3} = \mathbf{1}[\text{applied to R3 lottery}]$

    \vskip0.8ex
    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}
    \begin{tabular}{lrrrrr}
      \toprule
      Specification & $N$ & $\hat\delta$ & SE & $t$ & $p$ \\
      \midrule
      K\,=\,6, with loser ctrl  & 12,388 & $+0.051$ & 0.029 & 1.75 & 0.081 \\
      K\,=\,10, with loser ctrl & 12,388 & $+0.081$ & 0.043 & 1.90 & 0.058 \\
      \midrule
      \textbf{Priority subsample, K\,=\,6}
        & \textbf{6,402} & $\mathbf{+0.119}$ & \textbf{0.051}
        & \textbf{2.36} & \textbf{0.019} \\
      \bottomrule
      \multicolumn{6}{l}{\footnotesize State-clustered SE.\;
        Controls: log enroll., log income, poverty,}\\
      \multicolumn{6}{l}{\footnotesize \%\,white, PM$_{2.5}$, \%\,Dem\,2020,
        priority\,$\times$\,state FE.}\\
    \end{tabular}
    \end{adjustbox}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Interpretation:} An additional R1-winning neighbor raises own R3
    application probability by $\approx\!3$\,pp (full) to $\approx\!7$\,pp
    (priority districts).
  \end{alertblock}

  \vskip2ex

  %-- OLS vs 2SLS -------------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{OLS Naive vs.\ Structural 2SLS}

    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}
    \begin{tabular}{lrrrrr}
      \toprule
      Estimator & $\hat\beta$ & SE & $p$ & AR $p(\beta\!=\!0)$ & AR 95\% CI \\
      \midrule
      OLS (naive)          & $-0.040$ & 0.011 & $<$0.001 & — & — \\
      2SLS, full, K\,=\,6  & $+1.281$ & 0.928 & 0.167 & 0.087 & $[-0.18,\;7.03]$ \\
      2SLS, priority, K\,=\,6 & $+3.057$ & 2.093 & 0.144
        & \textbf{0.023} & $\mathbf{[+0.43,\;\infty)}$ \\
      \bottomrule
      \multicolumn{6}{l}{\footnotesize FS\,$F=7.06$ (K\,=\,6).\;
        AR\,=\,Anderson-Rubin weak-IV-robust CI.}\\
    \end{tabular}
    \end{adjustbox}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.2ex}
      \item \textbf{OLS sign flip} reveals selection bias: more-saturated
            local markets have lower marginal motivation to apply.
      \item \textbf{2SLS corrects} this; weak FS ($F\!=\!7.06$) makes AR
            CI the credible reference for inference.
      \item \textbf{Priority AR CI excludes zero}: structural effect is
            robustly positive even under weak-IV inference.
    \end{itemize}
  \end{block}

  \vskip2ex

  %-- Null benchmarks ---------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Null Benchmarks — Adoption Outcomes}
    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}
    \begin{tabular}{lrr}
      \toprule
      Outcome (K\,=\,6, loser ctrl) & $\hat\delta$ & $p$ \\
      \midrule
      CSBP adoption ITT          & $+0.007$ & 0.780 \\
      All-source WRI 2023--24    & $+0.018$ & 0.567 \\
      All-source WRI 2024 only   & $+0.004$ & 0.872 \\
      \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    \end{adjustbox}
    \vskip0.6ex
    {\small The peer effect is \textbf{specific to programme entry} —
    consistent with a window too short for deployment to drive observable
    adoption changes. Fiscal constraints may prevent interest from completing
    into ownership.}
  \end{block}

  \vskip2ex

  %-- Mechanism ---------------------------------------------------
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted title}{fg=white, bg=AmberGold}
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted body} {fg=black, bg=LightGrey}
  \begin{alertblock}{Mechanism: Timing-Sensitive Information Channel}

    \textbf{Sharp cutoff:} R3 deadline = October 2023.\\
    Split R1 deliveries: \textit{pre\_r3} ($\leq$2023\,Q3, \emph{visible})
    vs.\ \textit{post\_r3} ($\geq$2023\,Q4, \emph{invisible}).

    \vskip0.5ex
    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}
    \begin{tabular}{lrrrr}
      \toprule
      Timing & $\hat\eta$ & SE & $p$ & Direction \\
      \midrule
      \textit{pre\_r3} (visible)   & $+0.092$ & 0.054 & 0.091* & $\uparrow$ \\
      \textit{post\_r3} (invisible) & $-0.012$ & 0.072 & 0.865  & $\downarrow$ \\
      \midrule
      \multicolumn{5}{l}{\footnotesize Priority subsample.\;
        Wald (pre\,=\,post): $p = 0.239$.}\\
      \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    \end{adjustbox}

    \vskip0.5ex
    {\small Pre-deadline neighbors (buses \emph{visible} at time of decision)
    raise application rates; post-deadline neighbors do not.
    Post\_r3 is positive for \emph{adoption} outcomes — no generalised
    deterrence, only a deadline-sensitive information channel.}
  \end{alertblock}

\end{column}

%====================================================================
%  COLUMN 4 — Maps + Conclusions
%====================================================================
\begin{column}{\sepwid}\end{column}
\begin{column}{\onecolwid}

  %-- Program map -------------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Figure 2: R1 Winners and R3 Applicants}
    \begin{figure}
      \includegraphics[width=\linewidth,keepaspectratio]
        {map_01_national_overview.png}
      \caption{Panel A: R1 lottery winners (green). Panel B: R3 applicants
               who did not win R1 (orange). Application is concentrated in
               the South and Mid-Atlantic — identification relies on
               \emph{within-state, within-strata} variation.}
    \end{figure}
  \end{block}

  \vskip2ex

  %-- California zoom ---------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Figure 3: California — Delivery Timing and R3 Activity}
    \begin{figure}
      \includegraphics[width=\linewidth,keepaspectratio]
        {map_03_california_zoom.png}
      \caption{Left: R1 winner districts by delivery timing (green =
               pre-deadline; red = post-deadline). Right: R3 applicants.
               Pre-deadline deliveries are sparse; R3 application nonetheless
               occurs nearby, consistent with the information channel.}
    \end{figure}
  \end{block}

  \vskip2ex

  %-- Conclusions -------------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Conclusions \& Policy Implications}
    \begin{enumerate}\setlength\itemsep{0.5ex}
      \item \textbf{Peer effects at the application margin:} A lottery-winning
            neighbor raises R3 application propensity by $\sim$3--7\,pp
            (5--12\,pp for priority-eligible districts, $p<0.02$).
      \item \textbf{Structural effect positive for priority districts:}
            2SLS Anderson-Rubin CI excludes zero ($p=0.023$); OLS
            sign-flip confirms downward selection bias.
      \item \textbf{Timing-sensitive information channel:} Only
            \emph{pre-deadline} neighbor deployments generate spillovers;
            post-deadline buses have no detectable effect on application
            behavior.
      \item \textbf{No adoption spillovers (yet):} Null results for
            all-source WRI adoption suggest the 15-month window is too
            short for ownership-level peer effects to materialize.
    \end{enumerate}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Policy implication:} Expediting delivery and creating visible
    demonstration fleets could amplify federal ESB investment by triggering
    peer-induced demand in subsequent lottery rounds.

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textit{Next steps:} longer diffusion windows (2025--26 data);
    mechanism decomposition (vendor networks vs.\ direct information);
    heterogeneity by urbanicity.
  \end{block}

\end{column}
\begin{column}{\sepwid}\end{column}

\end{columns}

   156→
   157→    \vskip0.8ex
   158→    \textbf{This paper's fix — temporal design:}
   159→    Use \textbf{Round 1 (2022)} lottery randomness to predict neighbor bus
   160→    deployment \emph{visible} before \textbf{Round 3 (2023)} application
   161→    decisions.
   162→
   163→    \vskip1ex
   164→    \begin{center}
   165→    \begin{tikzpicture}[
   166→        node distance = 2.0cm,
   167→        box/.style   = {rectangle, rounded corners=4pt,

   174→      \node[box] (r1)  {R1 Lottery\\Oct 2022};

   176→      \node[box, right=of del] (r3)  {R3 Application\\Oct 2023};

   179→      \draw[arr] (del) -- node[above,lbl]{visibility} (r3);

   183→        (del.south) to

   189→
   190→    \vskip0.8ex
   191→    \textbf{Key validity conditions:}
   192→    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.1ex}
   193→      \item Lottery is random within \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} strata
   194→            (confirmed from program guide).
   195→      \item Neighbor loser-density control ($w_6$\,\textit{IS\_R1\_LOSER})
   196→            absorbs geographic application-clustering.
   197→      \item $Z$ affects $Y$ only through neighbor deployment (exclusion
   198→            restriction).
   199→    \end{itemize}
   200→  \end{block}
   201→
   202→  \vskip1.5ex
   203→
   204→  %-- Lottery structure -------------------------------------------
   205→  \begin{block}{Lottery Structure: 6-Tier Stratified Draw}
   206→    {\small Random \emph{within} \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} cells;
   207→    win rates differ \emph{between} cells by design.}
   208→
   209→    \vskip0.4ex
   210→    {\small
   211→    \begin{tabular}{@{}cl@{}}
   212→      \toprule Tier & Pool \\ \midrule
   213→      1 & ZE priority districts — per state \\
   214→      2 & Clean priority districts — per state \\
   215→      3 & All remaining priority districts \\
   216→      4 & Non-priority clean districts \\
   217→      5 & Remaining priority ZE \\
   218→      6 & Remaining non-priority ZE \\
   219→      \bottomrule
   220→    \end{tabular}
   221→    }
   222→
   223→    \vskip0.5ex
   224→    {\small$\Rightarrow$ FE: \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} interactions
   225→    ($\approx$100 dummies) for within-strata comparisons.}
   226→  \end{block}
   227→
   228→  \vskip1.5ex
   229→
   230→  %-- Estimating equations ----------------------------------------
   231→  \begin{block}{Estimating Equations}
   232→
   233→    \textbf{Reduced form (ITT):}
   234→    \vskip0.2ex
   235→    $Y_i^{R3} = \alpha + \delta\,\bar{Z}_i^{K=6} + \rho\,\bar{L}_i^{K=6}
   236→               + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s} + \varepsilon_i$
   237→
   238→    \vskip0.3ex
   239→    {\small $Y_i^{R3}=\mathbf{1}[\text{applied to R3}]$;\;
   240→    $\bar{Z}_i$ = neighbor R1 winner share;\;
   241→    $\bar{L}_i$ = neighbor R1 loser share.}
   242→
   243→    \vskip0.8ex
   244→    \textbf{Structural 2SLS:}
   245→    \vskip0.2ex
   246→    {\small FS:\;$\hat{D}_i = \pi\,\bar{Z}_i + \phi\,\bar{L}_i + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s}$}\\[0.3ex]
   247→    {\small SS:\;$Y_i^{R3} = \alpha + \beta^{\scriptscriptstyle IV}\hat{D}_i
   248→                 + \rho\,\bar{L}_i + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s} + u_i$}\\[0.2ex]
   249→    {\small $D_i$ = neighbor share with WRI-tracked ESB by end of 2023.}
   250→  \end{block}

   267→    \vskip0.8ex

   286→

   289→    application probability by $\approx\!3$\,pp (full) to $\approx\!7$\,pp
   290→    (priority districts).
   291→  \end{alertblock}
   292→
   293→  \vskip2ex
   294→
   295→  %-- OLS vs 2SLS -------------------------------------------------

   297→
   298→    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}
   299→    \begin{tabular}{lrrrrr}
   300→      \toprule
   301→      Estimator & $\hat\beta$ & SE & $p$ & AR $p(\beta\!=\!0)$ & AR 95\% CI \\
   302→      \midrule
   303→      OLS (naive)          & $-0.040$ & 0.011 & $<$0.001 & — & — \\
   304→      2SLS, full, K\,=\,6  & $+1.281$ & 0.928 & 0.167 & 0.087 & $[-0.18,\;7.03]$ \\

   311→    \end{adjustbox}
   312→
   313→    \vskip0.8ex
   314→    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.2ex}
   315→      \item \textbf{OLS sign flip} reveals selection bias: more-saturated
   316→            local markets have lower marginal motivation to apply.
   317→      \item \textbf{2SLS corrects} this; weak FS ($F\!=\!7.06$) makes AR
   318→            CI the credible reference for inference.
   319→      \item \textbf{Priority AR CI excludes zero}: structural effect is
   320→            robustly positive even under weak-IV inference.

   351→  \begin{alertblock}{Mechanism: Timing-Sensitive Information Channel}
   352→
   353→    \textbf{Sharp cutoff:} R3 deadline = October 2023.\\
   354→    Split R1 deliveries: \textit{pre\_r3} ($\leq$2023\,Q3, \emph{visible})
   355→    vs.\ \textit{post\_r3} ($\geq$2023\,Q4, \emph{invisible}).
   356→
   357→    \vskip0.5ex
   358→    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}
   359→    \begin{tabular}{lrrrr}

   364→      \textit{post\_r3} (invisible) & $-0.012$ & 0.072 & 0.865  & $\downarrow$ \\
   365→      \midrule

   415→  %-- Conclusions -------------------------------------------------
   416→  \begin{block}{Conclusions \& Policy Implications}
   417→    \begin{enumerate}\setlength\itemsep{0.5ex}
   418→      \item \textbf{Peer effects at the application margin:} A lottery-winning
   419→            neighbor raises R3 application propensity by $\sim$3--7\,pp
   420→            (5--12\,pp for priority-eligible districts, $p<0.02$).
   421→      \item \textbf{Structural effect positive for priority districts:}
   422→            2SLS Anderson-Rubin CI excludes zero ($p=0.023$); OLS
   423→            sign-flip confirms downward selection bias.
   424→      \item \textbf{Timing-sensitive information channel:} Only
   425→            \emph{pre-deadline} neighbor deployments generate spillovers;
   426→            post-deadline buses have no detectable effect on application
   427→            behavior.
   428→      \item \textbf{No adoption spillovers (yet):} Null results for
   429→            all-source WRI adoption suggest the 15-month window is too
   430→            short for ownership-level peer effects to materialize.
   431→    \end{enumerate}
   432→
   433→    \vskip0.8ex
   434→    \textbf{Policy implication:} Expediting delivery and creating visible
   435→    demonstration fleets could amplify federal ESB investment by triggering
   436→    peer-induced demand in subsequent lottery rounds.
   437→
   438→    \vskip0.8ex
   439→    \textit{Next steps:} longer diffusion windows (2025--26 data);
   440→    mechanism decomposition (vendor networks vs.\ direct information);
   441→    heterogeneity by urbanicity.
   442→  \end{block}

\begin{column}{\sepwid}\end{column}
\begin{column}{\onecolwid}

  %-- Motivation --------------------------------------------------
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted title}{fg=white, bg=BCMaroon}
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted body} {fg=black, bg=LightGrey}
  \begin{alertblock}{Why Electric School Buses?}
    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.2ex}
      \item $\approx\!500{,}000$ diesel school buses in the U.S.\ — the largest
            source of diesel pollution exposure for children.
      \item Federal \textbf{Clean School Bus Program} (CSBP, EPA, 2022):
            lottery-based rebates for electric/clean bus replacement.
      \item Adoption is geographically clustered (Figure~1) — some districts
            act early; most never apply. Why?
    \end{itemize}
    \vskip0.4em
    \textbf{Central question:} Does observing a \emph{neighbor district's}
    electric bus deployment increase your own probability of seeking adoption?
  \end{alertblock}

  \vskip2.5ex

  %-- Adoption history map ----------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Figure 1: ESB Adoption by District (All Sources)}
    \begin{figure}
      \includegraphics[width=\linewidth,keepaspectratio]
        {map_04_esb_adoption_history.png}
      \caption{First year of ESB adoption per district (WRI v9, June 2025).
               Yellow = early adopters ($\leq$2016); blue/purple = post-2022
               federal program. Only 1,361 of 13,221 CONUS districts have
               any ESB — adoption is sparse and geographically clustered.}
    \end{figure}
  \end{block}

  \vskip2.5ex

  %-- Literature --------------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Related Literature}
    {\small
    \textbf{Peer effects / social learning in adoption:}\\
    Conley \& Udry (2010); Bollinger \& Gillingham (2012);
    Noll et al.\ (2014); Bos et al.\ (2021)\\[0.5ex]
    \textbf{EV \& clean vehicle peer effects:}\\
    Muehlegger \& Wolfram (2023); Rode \& Weber (2016);
    Li et al.\ (2017); Chandra et al.\ (2010)\\[0.5ex]
    \textbf{Reflection problem \& IV strategies:}\\
    Manski (1993); Bram\-oulle et al.\ (2009);
    De Giorgi et al.\ (2010)\\[0.5ex]
    \textbf{Environmental \& energy program adoption:}\\
    Kahn \& Ketcham (2021); Ryan \& Tucker (2012);
    Gerarden et al.\ (2015); Fowlie et al.\ (2018)
    }
  \end{block}

\end{column}

%====================================================================
%  COLUMN 2 — Data + Identification
%====================================================================
\begin{column}{\sepwid}\end{column}
\begin{column}{\onecolwid}

  %-- Data (compact) ----------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Data}
    {\small
    \begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.38\linewidth}p{0.57\linewidth}@{}}
      \toprule
      \textbf{Source} & \textbf{Content} \\
      \midrule
      WRI ESB Dataset v9  & All-source ESB adoption; delivery dates \\
      EPA CSB Rebates     & R1 (2022) \& R3 (2023) lottery winners \\
      CSBP Applicants     & Waitlisted/rejected by round \\
      NCES EDGE           & District shapefiles + centroids \\
      NCES CCD / ACS      & Enrollment, income, poverty, race \\
      NASA SEDAC          & PM\textsubscript{2.5} \\
      MIT Election Lab    & 2020 county presidential vote \\
      \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    }
    \vskip0.5ex
    {\small\textbf{Sample:} 12,388 non-R1-winner districts.
    \textbf{Geography:} K\,=\,6 nearest neighbors (EPSG:5070).}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1.5ex

  %-- Identification ----------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Identification Challenge}
    \textbf{The reflection problem} (Manski, 1993): contemporaneous peer
    adoption is simultaneously determined — OLS is biased and inconsistent.

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{This paper's fix — temporal design:}
    Use \textbf{Round 1 (2022)} lottery randomness to predict neighbor bus
    deployment \emph{visible} before \textbf{Round 3 (2023)} application
    decisions.

    \vskip1ex
    \begin{center}
    \begin{tikzpicture}[
        node distance = 2.0cm,
        box/.style   = {rectangle, rounded corners=4pt,
                        draw=SlateBlue, fill=LightGrey,
                        text width=3.0cm, align=center,
                        minimum height=1.0cm, font=\small},
        arr/.style   = {-Stealth, thick, color=BCMaroon},
        lbl/.style   = {font=\footnotesize\itshape, color=SlateBlue}
      ]
      \node[box] (r1)  {R1 Lottery\\Oct 2022};
      \node[box, right=of r1]  (del) {R1 Bus\\Deliveries\\2022--2023};
      \node[box, right=of del] (r3)  {R3 Application\\Oct 2023};

      \draw[arr] (r1)  -- node[above,lbl]{$Z$: lottery} (del);
      \draw[arr] (del) -- node[above,lbl]{visibility} (r3);

      \draw[->, dashed, thick, color=ESBGreen,
            bend right=40, looseness=0.8]
        (del.south) to
        node[below, lbl, text width=2.8cm, align=center]
        {peer observes\\operating ESB}
        (r3.south);
    \end{tikzpicture}
    \end{center}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Key validity conditions:}
    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.1ex}
      \item Lottery is random within \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} strata
            (confirmed from program guide).
      \item Neighbor loser-density control ($w_6$\,\textit{IS\_R1\_LOSER})
            absorbs geographic application-clustering.
      \item $Z$ affects $Y$ only through neighbor deployment (exclusion
            restriction).
    \end{itemize}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1.5ex

  %-- Lottery structure -------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Lottery Structure: 6-Tier Stratified Draw}
    {\small Random \emph{within} \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} cells;
    win rates differ \emph{between} cells by design.}

    \vskip0.4ex
    {\small
    \begin{tabular}{@{}cl@{}}
      \toprule Tier & Pool \\ \midrule
      1 & ZE priority districts — per state \\
      2 & Clean priority districts — per state \\
      3 & All remaining priority districts \\
      4 & Non-priority clean districts \\
      5 & Remaining priority ZE \\
      6 & Remaining non-priority ZE \\
      \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    }

    \vskip0.5ex
    {\small$\Rightarrow$ FE: \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} interactions
    ($\approx$100 dummies) for within-strata comparisons.}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1.5ex

  %-- Estimating equations ----------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Estimating Equations}

    \textbf{Reduced form (ITT):}
    \vskip0.2ex
    $Y_i^{R3} = \alpha + \delta\,\bar{Z}_i^{K=6} + \rho\,\bar{L}_i^{K=6}
               + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s} + \varepsilon_i$

    \vskip0.3ex
    {\small $Y_i^{R3}=\mathbf{1}[\text{applied to R3}]$;\;
    $\bar{Z}_i$ = neighbor R1 winner share;\;
    $\bar{L}_i$ = neighbor R1 loser share.}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Structural 2SLS:}
    \vskip0.2ex
    {\small FS:\;$\hat{D}_i = \pi\,\bar{Z}_i + \phi\,\bar{L}_i + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s}$}\\[0.3ex]
    {\small SS:\;$Y_i^{R3} = \alpha + \beta^{\scriptscriptstyle IV}\hat{D}_i
                 + \rho\,\bar{L}_i + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s} + u_i$}\\[0.2ex]
    {\small $D_i$ = neighbor share with WRI-tracked ESB by end of 2023.}
  \end{block}

\end{column}

%====================================================================
%  COLUMN 3 — Results
%====================================================================
\begin{column}{\sepwid}\end{column}
\begin{column}{\onecolwid}

  %-- Main result -------------------------------------------------
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted title}{fg=white, bg=ESBGreen}
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted body} {fg=black, bg=LightGrey}
  \begin{alertblock}{Main Result: Application Margin (Estimand 2)}

    \textbf{Outcome:} $Y_i^{R3} = \mathbf{1}[\text{applied to R3 lottery}]$

    \vskip0.8ex
    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}
    \begin{tabular}{lrrrrr}
      \toprule
      Specification & $N$ & $\hat\delta$ & SE & $t$ & $p$ \\
      \midrule
      K\,=\,6, with loser ctrl  & 12,388 & $+0.051$ & 0.029 & 1.75 & 0.081 \\
      K\,=\,10, with loser ctrl & 12,388 & $+0.081$ & 0.043 & 1.90 & 0.058 \\
      \midrule
      \textbf{Priority subsample, K\,=\,6}
        & \textbf{6,402} & $\mathbf{+0.119}$ & \textbf{0.051}
        & \textbf{2.36} & \textbf{0.019} \\
      \bottomrule
      \multicolumn{6}{l}{\footnotesize State-clustered SE.\;
        Controls: log enroll., log income, poverty,}\\
      \multicolumn{6}{l}{\footnotesize \%\,white, PM$_{2.5}$, \%\,Dem\,2020,
        priority\,$\times$\,state FE.}\\
    \end{tabular}
    \end{adjustbox}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Interpretation:} An additional R1-winning neighbor raises own R3
    application probability by $\approx\!3$\,pp (full) to $\approx\!7$\,pp
    (priority districts).
  \end{alertblock}

  \vskip1ex

  %-- OLS vs 2SLS -------------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{OLS Naive vs.\ Structural 2SLS}

    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}
    \begin{tabular}{lrrrrr}
      \toprule
      Estimator & $\hat\beta$ & SE & $p$ & AR $p(\beta\!=\!0)$ & AR 95\% CI \\
      \midrule
      OLS (naive)          & $-0.040$ & 0.011 & $<$0.001 & — & — \\
      2SLS, full, K\,=\,6  & $+1.281$ & 0.928 & 0.167 & 0.087 & $[-0.18,\;7.03]$ \\
      2SLS, priority, K\,=\,6 & $+3.057$ & 2.093 & 0.144
        & \textbf{0.023} & $\mathbf{[+0.43,\;\infty)}$ \\
      \bottomrule
      \multicolumn{6}{l}{\footnotesize FS\,$F=7.06$ (K\,=\,6).\;
        AR\,=\,Anderson-Rubin weak-IV-robust CI.}\\
    \end{tabular}
    \end{adjustbox}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.2ex}
      \item \textbf{OLS sign flip} reveals selection bias: more-saturated
            local markets have lower marginal motivation to apply.
      \item \textbf{2SLS corrects} this; weak FS ($F\!=\!7.06$) makes AR
            CI the credible reference for inference.
      \item \textbf{Priority AR CI excludes zero}: structural effect is
            robustly positive even under weak-IV inference.
    \end{itemize}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1ex

  %-- Null benchmarks ---------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Null Benchmarks — Adoption Outcomes}
    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}
    \begin{tabular}{lrr}
      \toprule
      Outcome (K\,=\,6, loser ctrl) & $\hat\delta$ & $p$ \\
      \midrule
      CSBP adoption ITT          & $+0.007$ & 0.780 \\
      All-source WRI 2023--24    & $+0.018$ & 0.567 \\
      All-source WRI 2024 only   & $+0.004$ & 0.872 \\
      \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    \end{adjustbox}
    \vskip0.6ex
    {\small The peer effect is \textbf{specific to programme entry} —
    consistent with a window too short for deployment to drive observable
    adoption changes. Fiscal constraints may prevent interest from completing
    into ownership.}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1ex

  %-- Mechanism ---------------------------------------------------
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted title}{fg=white, bg=AmberGold}
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted body} {fg=black, bg=LightGrey}
  \begin{alertblock}{Mechanism: Timing-Sensitive Information Channel}

    \textbf{Sharp cutoff:} R3 deadline = October 2023.\\
    Split R1 deliveries: \textit{pre\_r3} ($\leq$2023\,Q3, \emph{visible})
    vs.\ \textit{post\_r3} ($\geq$2023\,Q4, \emph{invisible}).

    \vskip0.5ex
    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}
    \begin{tabular}{lrrrr}
      \toprule
      Timing & $\hat\eta$ & SE & $p$ & Direction \\
      \midrule
      \textit{pre\_r3} (visible)   & $+0.092$ & 0.054 & 0.091* & $\uparrow$ \\
      \textit{post\_r3} (invisible) & $-0.012$ & 0.072 & 0.865  & $\downarrow$ \\
      \midrule
      \multicolumn{5}{l}{\footnotesize Priority subsample.\;
        Wald (pre\,=\,post): $p = 0.239$.}\\
      \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    \end{adjustbox}

    \vskip0.5ex
    {\small Pre-deadline neighbors (buses \emph{visible} at time of decision)
    raise application rates; post-deadline neighbors do not.
    Post\_r3 is positive for \emph{adoption} outcomes — no generalised
    deterrence, only a deadline-sensitive information channel.}
  \end{alertblock}

\end{column}

%====================================================================
%  COLUMN 4 — Maps + Conclusions
%====================================================================
\begin{column}{\sepwid}\end{column}
\begin{column}{\onecolwid}

  %-- Program map -------------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Figure 2: R1 Winners and R3 Applicants}
    \begin{figure}
      \includegraphics[width=\linewidth,keepaspectratio]
        {map_01_national_overview.png}
      \caption{Panel A: R1 lottery winners (green). Panel B: R3 applicants
               who did not win R1 (orange). Application is concentrated in
               the South and Mid-Atlantic — identification relies on
               \emph{within-state, within-strata} variation.}
    \end{figure}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1ex

  %-- California zoom ---------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Figure 3: California — Delivery Timing and R3 Activity}
    \begin{figure}
      \centering
      \includegraphics[width=0.65\linewidth,keepaspectratio]
        {map_03_california_zoom.png}
      \caption{Left: R1 winner districts by delivery timing (green =
               pre-deadline; red = post-deadline). Right: R3 applicants.
               Pre-deadline deliveries are sparse; R3 application nonetheless
               occurs nearby, consistent with the information channel.}
    \end{figure}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1ex

  %-- Conclusions -------------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Conclusions \& Policy Implications}
    \begin{enumerate}\setlength\itemsep{0.5ex}
      \item \textbf{Peer effects at the application margin:} A lottery-winning
            neighbor raises R3 application propensity by $\sim$3--7\,pp
            (5--12\,pp for priority-eligible districts, $p<0.02$).
      \item \textbf{Structural effect positive for priority districts:}
            2SLS Anderson-Rubin CI excludes zero ($p=0.023$); OLS
            sign-flip confirms downward selection bias.
      \item \textbf{Timing-sensitive information channel:} Only
            \emph{pre-deadline} neighbor deployments generate spillovers;
            post-deadline buses have no detectable effect on application
            behavior.
      \item \textbf{No adoption spillovers (yet):} Null results for
            all-source WRI adoption suggest the 15-month window is too
            short for ownership-level peer effects to materialize.
    \end{enumerate}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Policy implication:} Expediting delivery and creating visible
    demonstration fleets could amplify federal ESB investment by triggering
    peer-induced demand in subsequent lottery rounds.

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textit{Next steps:} longer diffusion windows (2025--26 data);
    mechanism decomposition (vendor networks vs.\ direct information);
    heterogeneity by urbanicity.
  \end{block}

\end{column}
\begin{column}{\sepwid}\end{column}

\end{columns}
\end{frame}
\end{document}

```python
"""
map_01_national_overview.py
============================
Single combined national choropleth:
  - R1 lottery winner districts (green, 2022) — treatment
  - R3 applicant districts (orange, 2023) — outcome
  Both shown on the same map; by design R3 applicants exclude R1 winners,
  so the two colours are essentially non-overlapping (rare both→navy).

Output: 3_Output/Figures/map_01_national_overview.png  (150 dpi, poster-ready)
"""
import sys, io, warnings
if sys.stdout.encoding and sys.stdout.encoding.lower() != "utf-8":
    sys.stdout = io.TextIOWrapper(sys.stdout.buffer, encoding="utf-8")
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

import pandas as pd
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent))
from config import ANALYSIS_DATASET, SHP_FILE, FIGURES_DIR

# ── colors ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
C_R1   = "#1a7d40"   # deep green   — R1 winners (treatment)
C_R3   = "#e67e22"   # burnt orange — R3 applicants (outcome)
C_BOTH = "#1a3a5c"   # dark navy    — R1 winner + R3 applicant
C_NONE = "#d8d8d8"   # light grey   — no activity
C_BG   = "#f0f4f8"   # panel background

EXCLUDE_FIPS = {"02", "15", "60", "66", "69", "72", "78"}
CONUS_XLIM   = (-2.45e6, 2.35e6)
CONUS_YLIM   = (1.5e5,   3.30e6)


def load_data():
    shp = gpd.read_file(SHP_FILE)
    shp = shp.rename(columns={"GEOID": "nces_id"})
    shp["nces_id"] = shp["nces_id"].str.zfill(7)
    shp["fips2_pre"] = shp["nces_id"].str[:2]
    shp = shp[~shp["fips2_pre"].isin(EXCLUDE_FIPS)].copy()
    shp = shp.to_crs(epsg=5070)
    shp["geometry"] = shp.geometry.simplify(500)

    df = pd.read_csv(ANALYSIS_DATASET, low_memory=False, dtype={"nces_id": str})
    df["nces_id"] = df["nces_id"].str.zfill(7)

    def classify(row):
        r1, r3 = row["IV_Z_R1"], row["Y_R3_apply"]
        if r1 == 1 and r3 == 1: return "both"
        if r1 == 1:             return "r1_only"
        if r3 == 1:             return "r3_only"
        return "none"

    df["category"] = df.apply(classify, axis=1)

    gdf = shp[["nces_id", "geometry"]].merge(
        df[["nces_id", "IV_Z_R1", "Y_R3_apply", "category"]],
        on="nces_id", how="left"
    )
    gdf["category"] = gdf["category"].fillna("none")
    gdf["fips2"] = gdf["nces_id"].str[:2]
    gdf_conus = gdf[~gdf["fips2"].isin(EXCLUDE_FIPS)].copy()

    states = gdf_conus.dissolve(by="fips2").reset_index()[["fips2", "geometry"]]
    return gdf_conus, states, df


def main():
    print("Loading data...")
    gdf_conus, states, df = load_data()

    n_r1   = int((df["IV_Z_R1"] == 1).sum())
    n_r3   = int((df["Y_R3_apply"] == 1).sum())
    n_both = int(((df["IV_Z_R1"] == 1) & (df["Y_R3_apply"] == 1)).sum())
    print(f"  CONUS districts: {len(gdf_conus):,}")
    print(f"  R1 winners:      {n_r1}")
    print(f"  R3 applicants:   {n_r3}  (non-R1)")
    print(f"  Both:            {n_both}")

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=(14, 9), dpi=150, facecolor="white")
    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.01, right=0.99, top=0.88, bottom=0.10)

    ax.set_facecolor(C_BG)
    ax.set_xlim(*CONUS_XLIM)
    ax.set_ylim(*CONUS_YLIM)
    ax.axis("off")

    # 1. Grey base — all districts
    gdf_conus.plot(ax=ax, color=C_NONE, linewidth=0.0, edgecolor="none", zorder=1)

    # 2. State outlines
    states.boundary.plot(ax=ax, linewidth=0.55, edgecolor="#888888", zorder=2)

    # 3. R3 applicants (outcome) — drawn first so R1 winners appear on top
    r3 = gdf_conus[gdf_conus["category"] == "r3_only"]
    if len(r3):
        r3.plot(ax=ax, color=C_R3, linewidth=0.5, edgecolor="white", zorder=3)

    # 4. R1 winners (treatment)
    r1 = gdf_conus[gdf_conus["category"] == "r1_only"]
    if len(r1):
        r1.plot(ax=ax, color=C_R1, linewidth=0.5, edgecolor="white", zorder=4)

    # 5. Rare both — top layer
    both = gdf_conus[gdf_conus["category"] == "both"]
    if len(both):
        both.plot(ax=ax, color=C_BOTH, linewidth=0.5, edgecolor="white", zorder=5)

    # ── legend ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    handles = [
        mpatches.Patch(color=C_R1,   label=f"R1 lottery winner — treatment (N\u202f=\u202f{n_r1})"),
        mpatches.Patch(color=C_R3,   label=f"R3 applicant, non-R1 — outcome (N\u202f=\u202f{n_r3})"),
        mpatches.Patch(color=C_BOTH, label=f"R1 winner + R3 applicant (N\u202f=\u202f{n_both})"),
        mpatches.Patch(color=C_NONE, label="No program activity"),
    ]
    ax.legend(handles=handles, loc="lower left", fontsize=10,
              frameon=True, framealpha=0.9, edgecolor="#cccccc",
              bbox_to_anchor=(0.01, 0.02))

    ax.set_title(
        "R1 Lottery Winners (Treatment) and R3 Applicants (Outcome)\n"
        "Clean School Bus Program — CONUS Districts",
        fontsize=14, fontweight="bold", pad=10
    )

    FIGURES_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out = FIGURES_DIR / "map_01_national_overview.png"
    fig.savefig(out, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight", facecolor="white")
    print(f"\nSaved: {out}")
    plt.close(fig)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```python
"""
map_03_california_zoom.py
==========================
Single combined California map showing the delivery-timing mechanism:
  - R3 applicant districts (amber, non-R1) — outcome
  - R1 winner districts colored by delivery timing, overlaid — treatment:
      green  = pre_r3  (delivered ≤ 2023 Q3, visible before R3 deadline)
      red    = post_r3 (delivered ≥ 2023 Q4, invisible at R3 decision time)
      grey   = unknown delivery date

Seeing both layers on one map lets the viewer directly assess whether R3
applicants cluster near pre-deadline R1 deployments (the mechanism story).

Output: 3_Output/Figures/map_03_california_zoom.png  (150 dpi, poster-ready)
"""
import sys, io, warnings
if sys.stdout.encoding and sys.stdout.encoding.lower() != "utf-8":
    sys.stdout = io.TextIOWrapper(sys.stdout.buffer, encoding="utf-8")
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent))
from config import SPATIAL_DATASET, SHP_FILE, FIGURES_DIR, CSB_REBATES, WRI_BUS_EXCEL


# ── Colors ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
C_PRE_R3  = "#1a7d40"   # green  — visible before R3 deadline
C_POST_R3 = "#e74c3c"   # red    — arrived after R3 deadline
C_UNKNOWN = "#95a5a6"   # grey   — delivery date unknown
C_R3_APP  = "#f39c12"   # amber  — R3 applicant (non-R1)
C_NONE    = "#ececec"   # light grey — no activity


def build_delivery_categories():
    """Reconstruct the sharp delivery cutoff from WRI bus-level data."""
    reb = pd.read_excel(CSB_REBATES, dtype=str)
    reb.columns = reb.columns.str.strip().str.lower().str.replace(" ", "_")
    r1_ids = set(
        reb.loc[reb["funding_year"] == "2022", "nces_district_id"]
           .str.strip().str.zfill(7)
    )

    buses = pd.read_excel(WRI_BUS_EXCEL, sheet_name="2. Bus-level data", dtype=str)
    buses["nces_id"] = buses["1c. LEA ID"].str.strip().str.zfill(7)

    def parse_qtr(s):
        try:
            parts = str(s).strip().split()
            return int(parts[0]), int(parts[1].replace("Q", ""))
        except Exception:
            return np.nan, np.nan

    buses[["del_year", "del_q"]] = buses["3r. Quarter delivered"].apply(
        lambda x: pd.Series(parse_qtr(x))
    )

    def delivery_cat(row):
        y, q = row["del_year"], row["del_q"]
        if pd.isna(y):
            return "unknown"
        y, q = int(y), int(q)
        if y < 2023 or (y == 2023 and q <= 3):
            return "pre_r3"
        return "post_r3"

    buses["del_cat"] = buses.apply(delivery_cat, axis=1)

    r1_buses = buses[buses["nces_id"].isin(r1_ids)].copy()
    cat_order = {"pre_r3": 0, "post_r3": 1, "unknown": 2}
    r1_buses["cat_rank"] = r1_buses["del_cat"].map(cat_order)

    r1_del = (r1_buses.sort_values("cat_rank")
                      .groupby("nces_id")
                      .first()[["del_cat"]]
                      .rename(columns={"del_cat": "r1_del_cat"})
                      .reset_index())
    return r1_del


def main():
    print("Building delivery categories...")
    r1_del = build_delivery_categories()

    print("Loading spatial dataset...")
    sp = pd.read_csv(SPATIAL_DATASET, low_memory=False, dtype={"nces_id": str})
    sp["nces_id"] = sp["nces_id"].str.zfill(7)

    print("Loading shapefile...")
    shp = gpd.read_file(SHP_FILE)
    shp = shp.rename(columns={"GEOID": "nces_id"})
    shp["nces_id"] = shp["nces_id"].str.zfill(7)
    shp = shp.to_crs(epsg=5070)

    # California only (FIPS prefix 06)
    shp_ca = shp[shp["nces_id"].str.startswith("06")].copy()
    sp_ca  = sp[sp["nces_id"].str.startswith("06")].copy()

    df = sp_ca[["nces_id", "IV_Z_R1", "Y_R3_apply"]].merge(
        r1_del, on="nces_id", how="left"
    )

    def classify(row):
        if row["IV_Z_R1"] == 1:
            cat = row.get("r1_del_cat", np.nan)
            if cat == "pre_r3":  return "pre_r3"
            if cat == "post_r3": return "post_r3"
            return "r1_unknown"
        if row["Y_R3_apply"] == 1:
            return "r3_applicant"
        return "none"

    df["display_cat"] = df.apply(classify, axis=1)

    gdf = shp_ca[["nces_id", "geometry"]].merge(df, on="nces_id", how="left")
    gdf["display_cat"] = gdf["display_cat"].fillna("none")

    n_pre     = (gdf["display_cat"] == "pre_r3").sum()
    n_post    = (gdf["display_cat"] == "post_r3").sum()
    n_unk     = (gdf["display_cat"] == "r1_unknown").sum()
    n_r3      = (gdf["display_cat"] == "r3_applicant").sum()
    print(f"CA districts:        {len(gdf):,}")
    print(f"  pre_r3 R1:         {n_pre}")
    print(f"  post_r3 R1:        {n_post}")
    print(f"  R1 unknown timing: {n_unk}")
    print(f"  R3 applicants:     {n_r3}")

    # ── single combined map ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=(11, 11), dpi=150, facecolor="white")
    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.01, right=0.99, top=0.90, bottom=0.12)

    ax.set_facecolor("#dde8f0")
    ax.axis("off")

    # 1. Grey base
    gdf.plot(ax=ax, color=C_NONE, linewidth=0.12, edgecolor="#bbbbbb", zorder=1)

    # 2. R3 applicants (outcome) — amber, drawn below R1 timing layers
    r3 = gdf[gdf["display_cat"] == "r3_applicant"]
    if len(r3):
        r3.plot(ax=ax, color=C_R3_APP, alpha=0.9, linewidth=0.3,
                edgecolor="white", zorder=2)

    # 3. R1 winners by delivery timing — on top so they're clearly visible
    for cat, color, zord in [
        ("r1_unknown", C_UNKNOWN, 3),
        ("post_r3",    C_POST_R3, 4),
        ("pre_r3",     C_PRE_R3,  5),
    ]:
        sub = gdf[gdf["display_cat"] == cat]
        if len(sub):
            sub.plot(ax=ax, color=color, alpha=0.95, linewidth=0.4,
                     edgecolor="white", zorder=zord)

    # ── legend ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    legend_entries = [
        mpatches.Patch(color=C_PRE_R3,
                       label=f"R1 winner — pre-deadline delivery ($\\leq$2023 Q3) [N={n_pre}]"),
        mpatches.Patch(color=C_POST_R3,
                       label=f"R1 winner — post-deadline delivery ($\\geq$2023 Q4) [N={n_post}]"),
        mpatches.Patch(color=C_UNKNOWN,
                       label=f"R1 winner — delivery date unknown [N={n_unk}]"),
        mpatches.Patch(color=C_R3_APP,
                       label=f"R3 applicant, non-R1 winner [N={n_r3}]"),
        mpatches.Patch(color=C_NONE,
                       label="No program activity"),
    ]
    ax.legend(handles=legend_entries, loc="lower left", fontsize=9,
              frameon=True, framealpha=0.92, edgecolor="#cccccc",
              bbox_to_anchor=(0.01, 0.01))

    ax.set_title(
        "California: R1 Delivery Timing and R3 Application Activity\n"
        "Do R3 applicants (amber) cluster near pre-deadline R1 deployments (green)?",
        fontsize=13, fontweight="bold", pad=10
    )

    out = FIGURES_DIR / "map_03_california_zoom.png"
    fig.savefig(out, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight", facecolor="white")
    print(f"\nSaved: {out}")
    plt.close(fig)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

\setbeamercolor{block body}         {fg=black,    bg=white}

\setbeamercolor{block alerted body} {fg=black,    bg=LightGrey}

% ── Metadata ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\title{Peer Effects in Electric School Bus Adoption: Evidence from a Federal Lottery}
\author{Anirudh Pisharam\texorpdfstring{\quad}{,\space}\texttt{pisharam@bc.edu}}
\institute{Boston College, Department of Economics}

\usecaptiontemplate{
  \small\structure{\insertcaptionname~\insertcaptionnumber:}
  \insertcaption}

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\begin{document}
\begin{frame}[t]
\begin{columns}[t]

%====================================================================
%  COLUMN 1 — Motivation + ESB adoption map + Literature
%====================================================================
\begin{column}{\sepwid}\end{column}
\begin{column}{\onecolwid}

  %-- Motivation --------------------------------------------------
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted title}{fg=white, bg=BCMaroon}
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted body} {fg=black, bg=LightGrey}
  \begin{alertblock}{Why Electric School Buses?}
    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.2ex}
      \item $\approx\!500{,}000$ diesel school buses in the U.S.\ — the largest
            source of diesel pollution exposure for children.
      \item Federal \textbf{Clean School Bus Program} (CSBP, EPA, 2022):
            lottery-based rebates for electric/clean bus replacement.
      \item Adoption is geographically clustered (Figure~1) — some districts
            act early; most never apply. Why?
    \end{itemize}
    \vskip0.4em
    \textbf{Central question:} Does observing a \emph{neighbor district's}
    electric bus deployment increase your own probability of seeking adoption?
  \end{alertblock}

\begin{column}{\sepwid}\end{column}
\begin{column}{\onecolwid}

  %-- Identification ----------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Identification Challenge}
    \textbf{The reflection problem} (Manski, 1993): contemporaneous peer
    adoption is simultaneously determined — OLS is biased and inconsistent.

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{This paper's fix — temporal design:}
    Use \textbf{Round 1 (2022)} lottery randomness to predict neighbor bus
    deployment \emph{visible} before \textbf{Round 3 (2023)} application
    decisions.

    \vskip1ex
    \begin{center}
    \begin{tikzpicture}[
        node distance = 5.0cm,
        box/.style   = {rectangle, rounded corners=4pt,
                        draw=SlateBlue, fill=LightGrey,
                        text width=5.0cm, align=center,
                        minimum height=1.0cm, font=\tiny},
        arr/.style   = {-Stealth, thick, color=BCMaroon},
        lbl/.style   = {font=\footnotesize\itshape, color=SlateBlue}
      ]
      \node[box] (r1)  {R1 Lottery\\Oct 2022};
      \node[box, right=of r1]  (del) {R1 Bus\\Deliveries\\2022--2023};
      \node[box, right=of del] (r3)  {R3 Application\\Oct 2023};

      \draw[arr] (r1)  -- node[above,lbl]{$Z$: lottery} (del);
      \draw[arr] (del) -- node[above,lbl]{visibility} (r3);

      \draw[->, dashed, thick, color=ESBGreen,
            bend right=40, looseness=0.8]
        (del.south) to
        node[below, lbl, text width=2.8cm, align=center]
        {peer observes\\operating ESB}
        (r3.south);
    \end{tikzpicture}
    \end{center}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Key validity conditions:}
    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.1ex}
      \item Lottery is random within \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} strata
            (confirmed from program guide).
      \item Neighbor loser-density control ($w_6$\,\textit{IS\_R1\_LOSER})
            absorbs geographic application-clustering.
      \item $Z$ affects $Y$ only through neighbor deployment (exclusion
            restriction).
    \end{itemize}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1.5ex

  %-- Lottery structure -------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Lottery Structure: 6-Tier Stratified Draw}
    {\small Random \emph{within} \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} cells;
    win rates differ \emph{between} cells by design.}

    \vskip0.4ex
    {\small
    \begin{tabular}{@{}cl@{}}
      \toprule Tier & Pool \\ \midrule
      1 & ZE priority districts — per state \\
      2 & Clean priority districts — per state \\
      3 & All remaining priority districts \\
      4 & Non-priority clean districts \\
      5 & Remaining priority ZE \\
      6 & Remaining non-priority ZE \\
      \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    }

    \vskip0.5ex
    {\small$\Rightarrow$ FE: \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} interactions
    ($\approx$100 dummies) for within-strata comparisons.}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1.5ex

  %-- Estimating equations ----------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Estimating Equations}

    \textbf{Reduced form (ITT):}
    \vskip0.2ex
    $Y_i^{R3} = \alpha + \delta\,\bar{Z}_i^{K=6} + \rho\,\bar{L}_i^{K=6}
               + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s} + \varepsilon_i$

    \vskip0.3ex
    {\small $Y_i^{R3}=\mathbf{1}[\text{applied to R3}]$;\;
    $\bar{Z}_i$ = neighbor R1 winner share;\;
    $\bar{L}_i$ = neighbor R1 loser share.}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Structural 2SLS:}
    \vskip0.2ex
    {\small FS:\;$\hat{D}_i = \pi\,\bar{Z}_i + \phi\,\bar{L}_i + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s}$}\\[0.3ex]
    {\small SS:\;$Y_i^{R3} = \alpha + \beta^{\scriptscriptstyle IV}\hat{D}_i
                 + \rho\,\bar{L}_i + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s} + u_i$}\\[0.2ex]
    {\small $D_i$ = neighbor share with WRI-tracked ESB by end of 2023.}
  \end{block}

\end{column}

%  COLUMN 3 — Results
%====================================================================
\begin{column}{\sepwid}\end{column}
\begin{column}{\onecolwid}

  %-- Main result -------------------------------------------------
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted title}{fg=white, bg=ESBGreen}
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted body} {fg=black, bg=LightGrey}
  \begin{alertblock}{Main Result: Application Margin}

    \textbf{Outcome:} $Y_i^{R3} = \mathbf{1}[\text{applied to R3 lottery}]$

    \vskip0.8ex
    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}
    \begin{tabular}{lrrrrr}
      \toprule
      Specification & $N$ & $\hat\delta$ & SE & $t$ & $p$ \\
      \midrule
      K\,=\,6, with loser ctrl  & 12,388 & $+0.051$ & 0.029 & 1.75 & 0.081 \\
      K\,=\,10, with loser ctrl & 12,388 & $+0.081$ & 0.043 & 1.90 & 0.058 \\
      \midrule
      \textbf{Priority subsample, K\,=\,6}
        & \textbf{6,402} & $\mathbf{+0.119}$ & \textbf{0.051}
        & \textbf{2.36} & \textbf{0.019} \\
      \bottomrule
      \multicolumn{6}{l}{\footnotesize State-clustered SE.\;
        Controls: log enroll., log income, poverty,}\\
      \multicolumn{6}{l}{\footnotesize \%\,white, PM$_{2.5}$, \%\,Dem\,2020,
        priority\,$\times$\,state FE.}\\
    \end{tabular}
    \end{adjustbox}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Interpretation:} An additional R1-winning neighbor raises own R3
    application probability by $\approx\!3$\,pp (full) to $\approx\!7$\,pp
    (priority districts).
  \end{alertblock}

  \vskip1ex

  %-- OLS vs 2SLS -------------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{OLS Naive vs.\ Structural 2SLS}

    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}
    \begin{tabular}{lrrrrr}
      \toprule
      Estimator & $\hat\beta$ & SE & $p$ & AR $p(\beta\!=\!0)$ & AR 95\% CI \\
      \midrule
      OLS (naive)          & $-0.040$ & 0.011 & $<$0.001 & — & — \\
      2SLS, full, K\,=\,6  & $+1.281$ & 0.928 & 0.167 & 0.087 & $[-0.18,\;7.03]$ \\
      2SLS, priority, K\,=\,6 & $+3.057$ & 2.093 & 0.144
        & \textbf{0.023} & $\mathbf{[+0.43,\;\infty)}$ \\
      \bottomrule
      \multicolumn{6}{l}{\footnotesize FS\,$F=7.06$ (K\,=\,6).\;
        AR\,=\,Anderson-Rubin weak-IV-robust CI.}\\
    \end{tabular}
    \end{adjustbox}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.2ex}
      \item \textbf{OLS sign flip} reveals selection bias: more-saturated
            local markets have lower marginal motivation to apply.
      \item \textbf{2SLS corrects} this; weak FS ($F\!=\!7.06$) makes AR
            CI the credible reference for inference.
      \item \textbf{Priority AR CI excludes zero}: structural effect is
            robustly positive even under weak-IV inference.
    \end{itemize}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1ex

  %-- Null benchmarks ---------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Null Benchmarks — Adoption Outcomes}
    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}
    \begin{tabular}{lrr}
      \toprule

      \midrule
      CSBP adoption ITT          & $+0.007$ & 0.780 \\
      All-source WRI 2023--24    & $+0.018$ & 0.567 \\
      All-source WRI 2024 only   & $+0.004$ & 0.872 \\
      \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    \end{adjustbox}
    \vskip0.6ex
    {\small The peer effect is \textbf{specific to programme entry} —
    consistent with a window too short for deployment to drive observable
    adoption changes. Fiscal constraints may prevent interest from completing
    into ownership.}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1ex

  %-- Mechanism ---------------------------------------------------
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted title}{fg=white, bg=AmberGold}
  \setbeamercolor{block alerted body} {fg=black, bg=LightGrey}
  \begin{alertblock}{Mechanism: Timing-Sensitive Information Channel}

    \textbf{Sharp cutoff:} R3 deadline = October 2023.\\
    Split R1 deliveries: \textit{pre\_r3} ($\leq$2023\,Q3, \emph{visible})
    vs.\ \textit{post\_r3} ($\geq$2023\,Q4, \emph{invisible}).

    \vskip0.5ex
    \begin{adjustbox}{width=\linewidth}
    \begin{tabular}{lrrrr}
      \toprule
      Timing & $\hat\eta$ & SE & $p$ & Direction \\
      \midrule
      \textit{pre\_r3} (visible)   & $+0.092$ & 0.054 & 0.091* & $\uparrow$ \\
      \textit{post\_r3} (invisible) & $-0.012$ & 0.072 & 0.865  & $\downarrow$ \\
      \midrule
      \multicolumn{5}{l}{\footnotesize Priority subsample.\;
        Wald (pre\,=\,post): $p = 0.239$.}\\
      \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    \end{adjustbox}

    \vskip0.5ex
    {\small Pre-deadline neighbors (buses \emph{visible} at time of decision)
    raise application rates; post-deadline neighbors do not.
    Post\_r3 is positive for \emph{adoption} outcomes — no generalised
    deterrence, only a deadline-sensitive information channel.}
  \end{alertblock}

\end{column}

  \vskip1ex

  %-- Conclusions -------------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Conclusions \& Policy Implications}
    \begin{enumerate}\setlength\itemsep{0.5ex}
      \item \textbf{Peer effects at the application margin:} A lottery-winning
            neighbor raises R3 application propensity by $\sim$3--7\,pp
            (5--12\,pp for priority-eligible districts, $p<0.02$).
      \item \textbf{Structural effect positive for priority districts:}
            2SLS Anderson-Rubin CI excludes zero ($p=0.023$); OLS
            sign-flip confirms downward selection bias.
      \item \textbf{Timing-sensitive information channel:} Only
            \emph{pre-deadline} neighbor deployments generate spillovers;
            post-deadline buses have no detectable effect on application
            behavior.
      \item \textbf{No adoption spillovers (yet):} Null results for
            all-source WRI adoption suggest the 15-month window is too
            short for ownership-level peer effects to materialize.
    \end{enumerate}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Policy implication:} Expediting delivery and creating visible
    demonstration fleets could amplify federal ESB investment by triggering
    peer-induced demand in subsequent lottery rounds.

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textit{Next steps:} longer diffusion windows (2025--26 data);
    mechanism decomposition (vendor networks vs.\ direct information);
    heterogeneity by urbanicity.
  \end{block}

   166→    decisions.

   198→      \item Lottery is random within \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} strata
   199→            (confirmed from program guide).
   200→      \item Neighbor loser-density control ($w_6$\,\textit{IS\_R1\_LOSER})

   237→
   238→    \textbf{Reduced form (ITT):}
   239→    \vskip0.2ex
   240→    $Y_i^{R3} = \alpha + \delta\,\bar{Z}_i^{K=6} + \rho\,\bar{L}_i^{K=6}
   241→               + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s} + \varepsilon_i$
   242→
   243→    \vskip0.3ex
   244→    {\small $Y_i^{R3}=\mathbf{1}[\text{applied to R3}]$;\;
   245→    $\bar{Z}_i$ = neighbor R1 winner share;\;
   246→    $\bar{L}_i$ = neighbor R1 loser share.}

   248→    \vskip0.8ex
   249→    \textbf{Structural 2SLS:}
   250→    \vskip0.2ex
   251→    {\small FS:\;$\hat{D}_i = \pi\,\bar{Z}_i + \phi\,\bar{L}_i + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s}$}\\[0.3ex]

   253→                 + \rho\,\bar{L}_i + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s} + u_i$}\\[0.2ex]
   254→    {\small $D_i$ = neighbor share with WRI-tracked ESB by end of 2023.}

   356→  \begin{alertblock}{Mechanism: Timing-Sensitive Information Channel}

   422→  \begin{block}{Conclusions \& Policy Implications}
   423→    \begin{enumerate}\setlength\itemsep{0.5ex}
   424→      \item \textbf{Peer effects at the application margin:} A lottery-winning
   425→            neighbor raises R3 application propensity by $\sim$3--7\,pp

   432→            post-deadline buses have no detectable effect on application
   433→            behavior.
   434→      \item \textbf{No adoption spillovers (yet):} Null results for
   435→            all-source WRI adoption suggest the 15-month window is too
   436→            short for ownership-level peer effects to materialize.

  \begin{block}{Identification Challenge}
    \textbf{The reflection problem} (Manski, 1993): contemporaneous peer
    adoption is simultaneously determined — OLS is biased and inconsistent.

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{This paper's fix — temporal design:}
    Use \textbf{Round 1 (2022)} lottery randomness to predict neighbor bus
    deployment \emph{visible} before \textbf{Round 3 (2023)} application
    decisions.

            (confirmed from program guide).
      \item Neighbor loser-density control ($w_6$\,\textit{IS\_R1\_LOSER})
            absorbs geographic application-clustering.
      \item $Z$ affects $Y$ only through neighbor deployment (exclusion
            restriction).
    \end{itemize}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1.5ex

  %-- Lottery structure -------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Lottery Structure: 6-Tier Stratified Draw}
    {\small Random \emph{within} \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} cells;
    win rates differ \emph{between} cells by design.}

    \vskip0.4ex
    {\footnotesize
    \begin{tabular}{@{}cl@{}}
      \toprule Tier & Pool \\ \midrule
      1 & ZE priority districts — per state \\
      2 & Clean priority districts — per state \\
      3 & All remaining priority districts \\
      4 & Non-priority clean districts \\
      5 & Remaining priority ZE \\
      6 & Remaining non-priority ZE \\
      \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}

    \vskip0.5ex

    ($\approx$100 dummies) for within-strata comparisons.}
  \end{block}
