  %-- Estimating equations ----------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Estimating Equations}

    \textbf{Reduced form (ITT):}
    \vskip0.2ex
    $Y_i^{R3} = \alpha + \delta\,\bar{Z}_i^{K=6} + \rho\,\bar{L}_i^{K=6}
               + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s} + \varepsilon_i$

    \vskip0.3ex
    {\small $Y_i^{R3}=\mathbf{1}[\text{applied to R3}]$;\;
    $\bar{Z}_i$ = neighbor R1 winner share;\;
    $\bar{L}_i$ = neighbor R1 loser share.}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Structural 2SLS:}
    \vskip0.2ex
    {\small FS:\;$\hat{D}_i = \pi\,\bar{Z}_i + \phi\,\bar{L}_i + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s}$}\\[0.3ex]
    {\small SS:\;$Y_i^{R3} = \alpha + \beta^{\scriptscriptstyle IV}\hat{D}_i
                 + \rho\,\bar{L}_i + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s} + u_i$}\\[0.2ex]
    {\small $D_i$ = neighbor share with WRI-tracked ESB by end of 2023.}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1.5ex

  %-- OLS vs 2SLS -------------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{OLS Naive vs.\ Structural 2SLS}

    {\footnotesize
    \setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}lrrrrr@{}}
      \toprule
      Estimator & $\hat\beta$ & SE & $p$ & AR $p$ & AR 95\% CI \\
      \midrule
      OLS (naive)              & $-0.040$ & 0.011 & $<$0.001 & —     & — \\
      2SLS, full, K\,=\,6      & $+1.281$ & 0.928 & 0.167    & 0.087 & $[-0.18,\;7.03]$ \\
      2SLS, priority, K\,=\,6  & $+3.057$ & 2.093 & 0.144
        & \textbf{0.023} & $\mathbf{[+0.43,\;\infty)}$ \\
      \bottomrule
      \multicolumn{6}{l}{\scriptsize FS\,$F=7.06$ (K\,=\,6). AR\,=\,Anderson-Rubin weak-IV-robust CI.}\\
    \end{tabular}
    }

    \vskip0.8ex
    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.2ex}
      \item \textbf{OLS sign flip} reveals selection bias: more-saturated
            markets have lower marginal motivation to apply.
      \item \textbf{2SLS corrects} this; weak FS makes Anderson-Rubin CI
            the credible reference for inference.
      \item \textbf{Priority AR CI excludes zero}: structural effect is
            robustly positive under weak-IV inference.
    \end{itemize}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1ex

  %-- Conclusions -------------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Conclusions \& Policy Implications}
    \begin{enumerate}\setlength\itemsep{0.5ex}
      \item \textbf{Peer effects at the application margin:} A lottery-winning
            neighbor raises R3 application propensity by $\sim$3--7\,pp
            (5--12\,pp for priority-eligible districts, $p<0.02$).
      \item \textbf{Structural effect positive for priority districts:}
            2SLS Anderson-Rubin CI excludes zero ($p=0.023$); OLS
            sign-flip confirms downward selection bias.
      \item \textbf{Timing-sensitive information channel:} Only
            \emph{pre-deadline} neighbor deployments generate spillovers;
            post-deadline buses have no detectable effect on application
            behavior.
      \item \textbf{No adoption spillovers (yet):} Null results for
            all-source WRI adoption suggest the 15-month window is too
            short for ownership-level peer effects to materialize.
    \end{enumerate}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Policy implication:} Expediting delivery and creating visible
    demonstration fleets could amplify federal ESB investment by triggering
    peer-induced demand in subsequent lottery rounds.

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textit{Next steps:} longer diffusion windows (2025--26 data);
    mechanism decomposition (vendor networks vs.\ direct information);
    heterogeneity by urbanicity.

Here's an alternative summary (and questions/comments) from another LLM chat. Evaluate and let me know if these are valid points/concerns: Overall Assessment
The poster tells a coherent, well-structured story — temporal IV design, clear mechanism, honest null adoptions. The layout is clean and the priority-subsample result (δ=0.119, p=0.019, AR CI excludes zero) is a legitimate highlight. A few things need attention:

Issues / Inconsistencies with the Latest Results
1. OLS SE and p-value in the 2SLS Table — Major Error
The poster reports OLS naive: β=−0.040, SE=0.011, p<0.001.
But the current log (estimand_2sls.txt:21) gives: β=−0.040, SE=0.028, p=0.155 (state-clustered).

The poster appears to be reporting a non-clustered (HC) SE for the OLS row while the 2SLS rows use state-clustered SE — an internally inconsistent table. With clustered SE, OLS is not statistically significant. The sign-flip narrative remains valid, but claiming p<0.001 for OLS will raise reviewer flags instantly.

Fix: Re-run OLS with cov_type='cluster' consistently and update the table.

2. Effect Size Interpretation is Wrong — Moderate Error
The Main Result alert block says:

"An additional R1-winning neighbor raises own R3 application probability by ≈3 pp (full) to ≈7 pp (priority)."

But per the log's own interpretation note, δ directly equals the per-one-additional-winner-neighbor effect (a 1/K increase in share). That means:

Full, K=6: δ = +5.1 pp
Priority, K=6: δ = +11.9 pp
"3 pp to 7 pp" doesn't match any specification in the current results. This looks like a holdover from an older run.

Fix: Update to "≈5 pp (full) to ≈12 pp (priority)."

3. AR Confidence Interval Notation — Minor
The poster shows the priority AR 95% CI as [+0.43, ∞).
The log (estimand_2sls.txt:141) shows [0.425, 20.000] — 20 is the grid ceiling, not true infinity. A reviewer could legitimately object to claiming an infinite upper bound.

Fix: Write "[+0.43, >(grid)]" or add a footnote noting the grid upper bound is 20 and the CI is open above.

4. Sample Size Note is Inconsistent with Null Benchmarks — Minor
The Data block says "12,388 non-R1-winner districts," which matches the main result. But the Null Benchmark "CSBP adoption ITT" comes from Estimand 1, which uses N=12,721 (estimand1_itt.txt:3). No footnote distinguishes these.

Fix: Add "(N=12,721, includes all CSBP applicants)" to the CSBP ITT row in the Null Benchmarks table.

5. Mechanism Evidence is Stated More Confidently Than the Stats Warrant
The Mechanism alert block says: "pre-deadline neighbors raise application rates; post-deadline buses have no detectable effect." The Wald test footer (p=0.239) is there, but the prose doesn't acknowledge that the pre/post difference is not statistically distinguishable. The pattern is the right sign, but it's directional evidence, not a sharp test.

Fix: Soften the narrative: e.g., "Consistent with an information channel — pre-deadline coefficient is positive and marginally significant (p=0.091); post-deadline is null (p=0.865); Wald equality test p=0.239."

Structural / Story-Level Notes

  \begin{alertblock}{Why Electric School Buses?}
    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.2ex}

            source of diesel pollution exposure for children.
      \item Federal \textbf{Clean School Bus Program} (CSBP, EPA, 2022):
            lottery-based rebates for electric/clean bus replacement.
      \item Adoption is geographically clustered (Figure~1) — some districts
            act early; most never apply. Why?
    \end{itemize}
    \vskip0.4em
    \textbf{Central question:} Does observing a \emph{neighbor district's}
    electric bus deployment increase your own probability of seeking adoption?
  \end{alertblock}

    }
  \end{block}

  \begin{block}{Data}
    {\small

\end{column}

%====================================================================
\begin{column}{\sepwid}\end{column}
\begin{column}{\onecolwid}

  %-- Identification ----------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Identification Challenge}
    \textbf{The reflection problem} (Manski, 1993): contemporaneous peer
    adoption is simultaneously determined — OLS is biased and inconsistent.

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{This paper's fix — temporal design:}
    Use \textbf{Round 1 (2022)} lottery randomness to predict neighbor bus
    deployment \emph{visible} before \textbf{Round 3 (2023)} application
    decisions.

    \vskip1ex
    \begin{center}
    \begin{tikzpicture}[
        node distance = 5.0cm,
        box/.style   = {rectangle, rounded corners=4pt,
                        draw=SlateBlue, fill=LightGrey,
                        text width=5.0cm, align=center,
                        minimum height=1.0cm, font=\tiny},
        arr/.style   = {-Stealth, thick, color=BCMaroon},
        lbl/.style   = {font=\footnotesize\itshape, color=SlateBlue}
      ]
      \node[box] (r1)  {R1 Lottery\\Oct 2022};
      \node[box, right=of r1]  (del) {R1 Bus\\Deliveries\\2022--2023};
      \node[box, right=of del] (r3)  {R3 Application\\Oct 2023};

      \draw[arr] (r1)  -- node[above,lbl]{$Z$: lottery} (del);
      \draw[arr] (del) -- node[above,lbl]{visibility} (r3);

      \draw[->, dashed, thick, color=ESBGreen,
            bend right=40, looseness=0.8]
        (del.south) to
        node[below, lbl, text width=5cm, align=center]
        {peer observes operating ESB}
        (r3.south);
    \end{tikzpicture}
    \end{center}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Key validity conditions:}
    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.1ex}
      \item Lottery is random within \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} strata
      \item Neighbor loser-density control ($w_6$\,\textit{IS\_R1\_LOSER})
            absorbs geographic application-clustering.
      \item $Z$ affects $Y$ only through neighbor deployment
    \end{itemize}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1.5ex

  %-- Lottery structure -------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Lottery Structure: 6-Tier Stratified Draw}
    {\small Random \emph{within} \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} cells;
    win rates differ \emph{between} cells by design.}

    \vskip0.4ex
    {\footnotesize
    \begin{tabular}{@{}cl@{}}
      \toprule Tier & Pool \\ \midrule
      1 & ZE priority districts — per state \\
      2 & Clean priority districts — per state \\
      3 & All remaining priority districts \\
      4 & Non-priority clean districts \\
      5 & Remaining priority ZE \\
      6 & Remaining non-priority ZE \\
      \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
    }

    \vskip0.5ex
    {\small$\Rightarrow$ FE: \texttt{priority\,$\times$\,state} interactions
    ($\approx$100 dummies) for within-strata comparisons.}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1.5ex

  %-- Estimating equations ----------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{Estimating Equations}

    \textbf{Reduced form (ITT):}
    \vskip0.2ex
    $Y_i^{R3} = \alpha + \delta\,\bar{Z}_i^{K=6} + \rho\,\bar{L}_i^{K=6}
               + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s} + \varepsilon_i$

    \vskip0.3ex
    {\small $Y_i^{R3}=\mathbf{1}[\text{applied to R3}]$;\;
    $\bar{Z}_i$ = neighbor R1 winner share;\;
    $\bar{L}_i$ = neighbor R1 loser share.}

    \vskip0.8ex
    \textbf{Structural 2SLS:}
    \vskip0.2ex
    {\small FS:\;$\hat{D}_i = \pi\,\bar{Z}_i + \phi\,\bar{L}_i + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s}$}\\[0.3ex]
    {\small SS:\;$Y_i^{R3} = \alpha + \beta^{\scriptscriptstyle IV}\hat{D}_i
                 + \rho\,\bar{L}_i + \beta'X_i + \lambda_{p\times s} + u_i$}\\[0.2ex]
    {\small $D_i$ = neighbor share with WRI-tracked ESB by end of 2023.}
  \end{block}

  \vskip1.5ex

  %-- OLS vs 2SLS -------------------------------------------------
  \begin{block}{OLS Naive vs.\ Structural 2SLS}

    {\footnotesize
    \setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}
    \begin{tabular}{@{}lrrrrr@{}}
      \toprule
      Estimator & $\hat\beta$ & SE & $p$ & AR $p$ & AR 95\% CI \\
      \midrule
      OLS (naive)              & $-0.040$ & 0.011 & $<$0.001 & —     & — \\
      2SLS, full, K\,=\,6      & $+1.281$ & 0.928 & 0.167    & 0.087 & $[-0.18,\;7.03]$ \\
      2SLS, priority, K\,=\,6  & $+3.057$ & 2.093 & 0.144
        & \textbf{0.023} & $\mathbf{[+0.43,\;\infty)}$ \\
      \bottomrule
      \multicolumn{6}{l}{\scriptsize FS\,$F=7.06$ (K\,=\,6). AR\,=\,Anderson-Rubin weak-IV-robust CI.}\\
    \end{tabular}
    }

    \vskip0.8ex
    \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.2ex}
      \item \textbf{OLS sign flip} reveals selection bias: more-saturated
            markets have lower marginal motivation to apply.
      \item \textbf{2SLS corrects} this; weak FS makes Anderson-Rubin CI
            the credible reference for inference.
      \item \textbf{Priority AR CI excludes zero}: structural effect is
            robustly positive under weak-IV inference.
    \end{itemize}
  \end{block}
